title: Sequences of Rigid Transformations Core Test
description: Apply ordered sequences of translations, reflections, and rotations; reason backward from images; and use rigid-motion sequences to justify congruence.

questions.questionText: Point A is (2, 3). Apply this sequence: translate by <4, -1>, then reflect across the x-axis. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (6, 2); after the second step A'' is (6, -2).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-3, 5). Apply this sequence: reflect across the y-axis, then translate by <2, -4>. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (3, 5); after the second step A'' is (5, 1).

questions.questionText: Point A is (4, -2). Apply this sequence: rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then translate by <1, 3>. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (-4, 2); after the second step A'' is (-3, 5).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-5, -1). Apply this sequence: translate by <3, 6>, then reflect across the y-axis. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (-2, 5); after the second step A'' is (2, 5).

questions.questionText: Point A is (1, -6). Apply this sequence: reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <-2, 5>. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (1, 6); after the second step A'' is (-1, 11).

questions.questionText: Point A is (6, 2). Apply this sequence: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then translate by <3, 0>. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (-2, 6); after the second step A'' is (1, 6).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-2, 4). Apply this sequence: rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, then reflect across the x-axis. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (4, 2); after the second step A'' is (4, -2).

questions.questionText: Point A is (3, -5). Apply this sequence: translate by <-4, 2>, then rotate 180 degrees about the origin. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (-1, -3); after the second step A'' is (1, 3).

questions.questionText: Point A is (0, 7). Apply this sequence: reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (0, -7); after the second step A'' is (-7, 0).

questions.questionText: Point A is (-6, 0). Apply this sequence: reflect across the y-axis, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What is A''?
questions.explanation: Apply the steps in order. After the first step A is (6, 0); after the second step A'' is (0, 6).

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (2, -4) to (3, 7)?
options: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then translate by <5, 1>
reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <5, 1>
translate by <5, 1>, then translate by <1, -1>
translate by <5, 1>, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin
questions.correctAnswer: translate by <5, 1>, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (-4, 3) to (2, 10)?
options: translate by <-1, 6>, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin
reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin
rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, then translate by <-1, 6>
rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, then translate by <1, -1>
questions.correctAnswer: rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, then translate by <-1, 6>
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (5, 1) to (-5, 1)?
options: rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then reflect across the x-axis
reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 180 degrees about the origin
reflect across the x-axis, then reflect across the x-axis
reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <1, -1>
questions.correctAnswer: reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 180 degrees about the origin
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (-2, -7) to (-2, 7)?
options: rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then reflect across the y-axis
reflect across the y-axis, then rotate 180 degrees about the origin
reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 180 degrees about the origin
rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then translate by <1, -1>
questions.correctAnswer: rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then reflect across the y-axis
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (7, -3) to (-4, 2)?
options: reflect across the y-axis, then translate by <-3, 5>
reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <-3, 5>
translate by <-3, 5>, then reflect across the y-axis
translate by <-3, 5>, then translate by <1, -1>
questions.correctAnswer: translate by <-3, 5>, then reflect across the y-axis
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (-1, 6) to (6, -1)?
options: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then reflect across the x-axis
reflect across the x-axis, then reflect across the x-axis
reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <1, -1>
reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin
questions.correctAnswer: reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (3, 4) to (-4, -3)?
options: reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin
rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then reflect across the x-axis
rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then translate by <1, -1>
questions.correctAnswer: rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin, then reflect across the x-axis
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: Which ordered sequence maps point (-6, 2) to (-3, 4)?
options: rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin, then translate by <2, -5>
reflect across the x-axis, then translate by <2, -5>
translate by <2, -5>, then translate by <1, -1>
translate by <2, -5>, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin
questions.correctAnswer: translate by <2, -5>, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin
questions.explanation: For a sequence of transformations, order matters. Test each step in order from the original point.

questions.questionText: A point is transformed by this sequence: translate by <3, 2>, then reflect across the x-axis. The final image is (1, -5). What was the original point?
questions.explanation: To find the preimage, undo the transformations in reverse order.

questions.questionText: A point is transformed by this sequence: reflect across the y-axis, then translate by <1, -2>. The final image is (4, 6). What was the original point?
questions.explanation: To find the preimage, undo the transformations in reverse order.

questions.questionText: A point is transformed by this sequence: rotate 180 degrees about the origin, then translate by <5, -1>. The final image is (-3, 2). What was the original point?
questions.explanation: To find the preimage, undo the transformations in reverse order.

questions.questionText: A point is transformed by this sequence: translate by <-2, 3>, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. The final image is (7, -4). What was the original point?
questions.explanation: To find the preimage, undo the transformations in reverse order.

questions.questionText: A point is transformed by this sequence: reflect across the x-axis, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. The final image is (-6, -1). What was the original point?
questions.explanation: To find the preimage, undo the transformations in reverse order.

questions.questionText: Why does a sequence of translations, reflections, and rotations preserve side lengths?
options: Only translations preserve length.
Each step is a rigid transformation.
The figure returns to the origin.
The coordinates always stay the same.
questions.correctAnswer: Each step is a rigid transformation.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A triangle is translated, reflected, and rotated. Which statement must be true about the final image?
options: It is always larger.
It is always in the same quadrant.
It is similar but never congruent.
It is congruent to the original triangle.
questions.correctAnswer: It is congruent to the original triangle.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which detail is most important when following a transformation sequence?
options: The alphabetic order of the vertices
The color of the figure
The order of the steps
The quadrant of the final image only
questions.correctAnswer: The order of the steps
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A sequence starts with a reflection and ends with a translation. What can change?
options: The measure of each angle
The length of each side
The figure's location and orientation
Whether corresponding sides are congruent
questions.correctAnswer: The figure's location and orientation
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which sequence is guaranteed to undo itself when repeated once more?
options: Translate by <3, 2>
Reflect across the x-axis
Rotate 90 degrees clockwise
Translate by <-1, 5>
questions.correctAnswer: Reflect across the x-axis
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A 90 degree clockwise rotation followed by a 90 degree counterclockwise rotation is equivalent to which move?
options: A 180 degree rotation
A reflection across the y-axis
No net movement
A translation right 1
questions.correctAnswer: No net movement
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: A student applies the second transformation before the first. What is the likely issue?
options: The final image must still be the same.
The final image may be different because order can matter.
The figure cannot be congruent anymore.
The question has no solution.
questions.correctAnswer: The final image may be different because order can matter.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which sequence must preserve angle measures?
options: Stretch, then rotate
Dilate by 2, then translate
Scale horizontally, then reflect
Reflect, then translate, then rotate
questions.correctAnswer: Reflect, then translate, then rotate
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: If P maps to P' and then P'' in a two-step sequence, what does P' represent?
options: The intermediate image after the first step
The original point
The final image after all steps
The center of rotation
questions.correctAnswer: The intermediate image after the first step
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Two different rigid-motion sequences map one triangle onto another. What does that show?
options: The triangles have different side lengths.
The second triangle must be larger.
The triangles are congruent.
The triangles cannot have equal angles.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles are congruent.
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which sequence is not made only of rigid transformations?
options: Translate, then dilate by 2
Reflect, then rotate
Translate, then reflect
Rotate, then translate
questions.correctAnswer: Translate, then dilate by 2
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: What is preserved through every sequence in this lesson?
options: Area only, not angles
Coordinates of every point
The quadrant of every vertex
Distance and angle measure
questions.correctAnswer: Distance and angle measure
questions.explanation: A sequence of rigid transformations is still rigid, so it preserves distances and angle measures.

questions.questionText: Point P(2, -3) is translated by <4, 1>, reflected across the y-axis, then rotated 180 degrees about the origin. Where is the final image?
questions.explanation: P becomes (6, -2), then (-6, -2), then (6, 2).

questions.questionText: Point P(-5, 4) is reflected across the x-axis, translated by <3, -2>, then rotated 90 degrees clockwise about the origin. Where is the final image?
questions.explanation: P becomes (-5, -4), then (-2, -6), then (-6, 2).

questions.questionText: A point is translated by <2, -5>, then translated by <-2, 5>. Which statement describes the combined move?
options: The point reflects across the origin.
The point rotates 180 degrees.
The point moves 4 units right and 10 units down.
The point returns to its original location.
questions.correctAnswer: The point returns to its original location.
questions.explanation: The two translation vectors are opposites, so they undo each other.

questions.questionText: Which sequence is equivalent to a 180 degree rotation about the origin?
options: Reflect across the x-axis, then reflect across the x-axis.
Translate by <2, 0>, then translate by <-2, 0>.
Rotate 90 degrees clockwise, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise.
Rotate 90 degrees clockwise, then rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise.
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate 90 degrees clockwise, then rotate 90 degrees clockwise.
questions.explanation: Two quarter-turns in the same direction make a half-turn.

questions.questionText: A triangle is transformed by three rigid motions. Which evidence best proves the final image is congruent to the original?
options: The image is in Quadrant I.
Corresponding side lengths and angle measures are equal.
The vertices have positive coordinates.
The sequence contains exactly three steps.
questions.correctAnswer: Corresponding side lengths and angle measures are equal.
questions.explanation: Congruence depends on preserved distance and angle measure, not location.

questions.questionText: Point P maps to P'' after a reflection across the y-axis and then a translation by <4, -1>. If P'' is (9, 2), what was P?
questions.explanation: Undo the translation first to get (5, 3), then undo the y-axis reflection to get (-5, 3).

questions.questionText: Point P maps to P'' after a 180 degree rotation and then a translation by <-3, 2>. If P'' is (4, -5), what was P?
questions.explanation: Undo the translation to get (7, -7), then undo the 180 degree rotation to get (-7, 7).

questions.questionText: A student claims that translating then reflecting always gives the same result as reflecting then translating. Which response is best?
options: Always true for all rigid transformations.
Never true for any point.
Only true if the point starts at the origin.
Not always; changing the order can change the final coordinates.
questions.correctAnswer: Not always; changing the order can change the final coordinates.
questions.explanation: Some transformations commute in special cases, but order cannot be assumed.

questions.questionText: Point A(1, 2) and B(5, 2) are transformed by the same sequence of rigid motions. What must be true about A''B''?
options: A''B'' is 8 units long.
A''B'' is 4 units long.
A''B'' is 2 units long.
A''B'' must lie on the x-axis.
questions.correctAnswer: A''B'' is 4 units long.
questions.explanation: The original segment length is 4, and rigid transformations preserve distance.

questions.questionText: A triangle is reflected and then rotated. What can happen to its orientation?
options: It must stay exactly the same.
It must double in size.
It can change, while size and angle measures stay the same.
Its angle measures must change.
questions.correctAnswer: It can change, while size and angle measures stay the same.
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations can change location and orientation without changing size or angle measures.

questions.questionText: Which sequence would prove two figures are congruent?
options: Dilate one figure by 3 to land on the other.
Translate one figure, rotate it, then reflect it to land exactly on the other.
Stretch one figure horizontally to match the other.
Change one angle so it matches the other.
questions.correctAnswer: Translate one figure, rotate it, then reflect it to land exactly on the other.
questions.explanation: A congruence proof can use only rigid transformations.

questions.questionText: Point P(3, 1) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise, reflected across the x-axis, then translated by <2, 4>. Where is the final image?
questions.explanation: P becomes (-1, 3), then (-1, -3), then (1, 1).

questions.questionText: A sequence sends every point of Figure A onto Figure B using only rigid transformations. Which conclusion is valid?
options: Figure A is larger than Figure B.
Figure A is similar but not congruent to Figure B.
Figure B must be a translation only.
Figure A is congruent to Figure B.
questions.correctAnswer: Figure A is congruent to Figure B.
questions.explanation: If rigid transformations map one figure exactly onto another, the figures are congruent.

questions.questionText: Which two-step sequence leaves every point exactly where it started?
options: Translate by <1, 1>, then translate by <1, 1>
Reflect across the y-axis, then reflect across the y-axis again
Rotate 90 degrees clockwise, then rotate 180 degrees
Reflect across the x-axis, then translate up 2
questions.correctAnswer: Reflect across the y-axis, then reflect across the y-axis again
questions.explanation: A reflection across the same line twice undoes itself.

questions.questionText: A square is translated, reflected, rotated, and reflected again. Which property is not guaranteed to stay the same?
options: The coordinates of each vertex
The length of each side
The measure of each angle
The area of the square
questions.correctAnswer: The coordinates of each vertex
questions.explanation: Rigid transformations may change coordinates while preserving size and shape.
